name: CHero_GetEffectiveMaxLife
comment:
CHero::GetEffectiveMaxLife -- verified byte-exact from 0x65D0C9..0x65D132 for the base and
profession chain, because HLIL renders the descending if-chain with a shared store address
and is ambiguous there.

OVERRIDE GATE
  A = (hero+0x514 > 0) && CGameMap_HasFlags64HighBit6_Analyst()
  B = CRole_HasTransformLook(hero)          ; role+0xEC != 0
  if (A || B) return hero+0x514;         ; note this can return 0 when !A && B
  ; i.e. the normal formula runs only when !A && !B

BASE
  base = (strength +0x4FC + agility +0x504 + vitality +0x508 * 8 + spirit +0x50C) * 3
         (lea edi,[eax+eax*2] after the three adds)

PROFESSION BONUS -- applies ONLY when (prof % 1000) / 10 == 1, i.e. professions 10..19
  t = prof % 10; pct = {1:5, 2:8, 3:10, 4:12, 5:15}, else 0
  base += (pct * base) / 100             ; SIGNED idiv, truncates toward zero

EQUIPMENT, slots 1..0x12 inclusive (i < 0x13), via CHeroItem__GetEquipSlotItemRef (shared_ptr)
  skip when CItem_IsBrokenOrDisabled(item)
  base += (int16)CItem_GetEffectiveLife(item)   ; movsx  @0x65D156
        + (uint16)*(item+0x180)                 ; movzx  @0x65D15B, the ItemAdd record cache
  if (slot != 0xC) base += CItem_GetEnchantmentLifeBonus(item)
  if (CItem_GetPrimaryRefinementEffectId(item) == 0x12D)   base += CItem_GetPrimaryRefinementValue(item)
  if (CItem_GetPrimaryRefinementEffectId(item) <  0x64 &&
      CItem_GetSecondaryRefinementEffectId(item) == 0x12D) base += CItem_GetSecondaryRefinementValue(item)

OVERLAY
  if (CGameMap_HasOverlayRenderModeFlag(map)) base += hero+0xCB0

TIER TABLE
  d = CHero_GetPackedPerTypeLevelDigit(hero, 9)
  if (d > 0 && d <= 9) base += table[d] where table = {0,100,200,300,400,500,600,800,1000,1200}
  (built as var_40=0 followed by a 9-dword memcpy, indexed as (&var_40)[d])

CLAMP
  return base >= 0 ? base : 0

item+0x180 is the ItemAdd record cache filled by CItem_RefreshItemAddRecordCache (0x67AC6B) via
GameDataSingleton_TryGetActionTypeRecordByDualKey(store, (normalizedType/10)*10,
CItem_GetByte61(item), item+0x180); the life term is that record's FIRST word.

Managed mirror: Conquer.World.State.ClientWorldLocalHeroMaxStatResolver; the equipment loop is
ClientWorldLocalHeroItemStatResolver. See 20_notes/Rendering/14_hero_effective_max_life_mana.md

CP2.2 revalidation 2026-11-06: raw x86 confirms the formula/branch constants above. The map predicate is qword bit 38 (high dword 0x40), not low 0x40. Override positivity uses unsigned JBE (nonzero raw dword); the returned override is an int32 bit pattern. See 20_notes/Rendering/hero-model-cp22.md.

name: CHero_GetEffectiveMaxMana
comment:
CHero::GetEffectiveMaxMana -- verified byte-exact from 0x65D285..0x65D318, because HLIL
renders the descending multiplier chain with a shared store address (0x65D2BD is reused by
the >=5, >=4 and >=2 arms) and cannot be read as written.

OVERRIDE GATE -- simpler than max life, and it does NOT consult role+0xEC
  if (hero+0x518 > 0 && CGameMap_HasFlags64HighBit6_Analyst()) return hero+0x518;

BASE
  spirit = hero+0x50C
  result = spirit * 5                    ; lea esi,[ecx+ecx*4], the DEFAULT

PROFESSION MULTIPLIER -- applies only when (prof % 1000) / 10 > 10  (UNSIGNED jbe skips <= 10)
  t = prof % 10                          ; SIGNED comparisons (jl)
  t >= 5 -> spirit * 30   (imul 0x1E)
  t >= 4 -> spirit * 25   (imul 0x19)
  t >= 3 -> spirit * 20   (lea *5 then shl 2)
  t >= 2 -> spirit * 15   (imul 0x0F)
  t >= 1 -> spirit * 10   (lea *5 then shl 1)
  t == 0 -> leaves the spirit * 5 default

Note the asymmetry with max life, which gates on == 1 rather than > 10 and applies a
percentage rather than replacing the multiplier.

EQUIPMENT -- 18 iterations from hero+0xE8C, stride 8, reading the RAW pointer
  (max life instead walks slots 1..0x12 through the shared_ptr accessor)
  if (*p) result += (int16)CItem_GetEffectiveMana(*p)     ; movsx ax

No overlay bonus and no tier table, unlike max life.

CLAMP
  return result >= 0 ? result : 0

See 20_notes/Rendering/14_hero_effective_max_life_mana.md

CP2.2 revalidation 2026-11-06: preserve unsigned profession-family gate, distinct multiplier arms, signed equipped mana, and final signed zero floor. Unlike life, transformation does not select the override. See 20_notes/Rendering/hero-model-cp22.md.

name: CHero_GetEffectiveMaxPhysicalForce
comment:
Returns hero+0x834, initialized to 100 at CHero_InitializeState:0x6570A9, or unsigned (value*3)>>1 when native status flag index 0x21 is set. With the native baseline this is 100 normally and 150 under the extended physical-force status. CDlgMain uses it as Progress46's live range.

CP2.2: raw initialization at 0x6570A9 stores 100 to +0x834; status helper 0x66F766 tests index 0x21 through Role_HasStatusFlag (0x6E50D4), i.e. low qword bit 33. LEA/SHR at 0x66F7A4/0x66F7A7 is uint32 wrapping (base*3)>>1, yielding 150 for baseline 100. No dynamic max-force input is established for the current managed projection.

name: CHero_GetCappedPhysicalForce
comment: CP2.2: +0x830 is compared with the effective maximum at 0x66F78A; JG at 0x66F78C is SIGNED. This is an upper-only int32 cap; high-bit current values are negative and are not floored to zero.

name: CMsgItem__Process
comment:
Subtype 17 reads tracked position at packet+4 and signed durability at packet+8. It always writes the incoming low word to CItem current durability. For non-positive durability it also sets CItem+0x1AC broken/disabled to 1 when the item is equipment-category; the positive path does not clear that byte. MsgItem update-existing is the verified path that explicitly rewrites the byte to 0 for positive durability.

Subtype 46 is the complete equipment snapshot. Packet offsets 0x20..0x50 map to equip slots 1..9,15..18 in order. Each UID is resolved through CHeroItem__FindTrackedItemByUid; missing/zero UIDs clear the corresponding slot. After CHero__RefreshEquipmentDerivedStats, native computes effective max life and uses signed comparison to clamp current life when current > max; it writes both player-data index 1 (current life) and index 15 (HP gauge follower) to max.

After the optional clamp, subtype 46 unconditionally posts WM_USER-style message 0x464 five times in this exact wParam order: 0x3EB, 0x3FB, 0x445, 0x446, 0x4FE. Every post has lParam 0. The receiver refreshes visible equipment-dependent dialogs and always refreshes item-shortcut stack counts for 0x3EB.

CP2.2 clamp revalidation: 0x6EC49A cmp eax,esi; 0x6EC49C JLE skips for current<=maximum under SIGNED int32 comparison. No maximum>=0 guard exists. On actual clamp, index1 and index15 both receive the same maximum (0x6EC4B8 and 0x6EC4C7). Equal/below-maximum cases do not reset the follower. Managed packet-batch/deferred-clamp ordering is a separate known gap; this annotation does not claim that gap is closed.

name: CHero_PerFrameTickAndSubsystemUpdate
comment:
Each tick advances the HUD's delayed HP and MP followers with signed 32-bit comparisons. If follower < current, add effectiveMax / 80 when effectiveMax >= 80, otherwise add 1; then clamp follower down to current if it overshoots. HP uses player-data index 15 (current life is index 1). MP uses protected fields CHero+0x768 (follower) and CHero+0x5E0 (current). Both followers snap down immediately when current falls.

CP2.2 revalidation: HP follower window 0x65E128..0x65E167 and MP window 0x65E1C9..0x65E24C use signed comparisons, signed max/80 when max>=80 else +1, wrapping add and signed min(current). Equipment-snapshot clamp separately writes HP follower index15 to max at 0x6EC4C7; it does not reset MP follower. See 20_notes/Rendering/hero-model-cp22.md.
